broken_pdf_links.result: The Legislature's linked PDF returned a 404 HTML page.
broken_pdf_links.recovery: The chapter HTML and all four current section pages, sections 44-2801 through 44-2804, were retrieved and searched separately.

searches.disposition: Both were unrelated references to federal, state, and local income-tax returns or pre-tax earnings.
One insurance exemption and one combined-employer withholding provision; neither grants municipal taxing authority.

searches.pattern: tax measured by wages, earnings, compensation, or payroll
searches.disposition: State unemployment-insurance financing, not a municipal employee tax.

searches.pattern: income tax within 500 characters of city or municipal terms, both directions
searches.disposition: All contexts were reviewed. They concern federal bond-interest exemptions, state income-tax programs, definitions, or other nonmunicipal subjects; none grants or describes a municipal income tax.

searches.pattern: municipal/city, tax/levy/impose/assess, and wages/earnings/compensation/payroll proximity permutations
searches.disposition: The candidate contexts were reviewed, with all Title 50 municipal-corporation hits examined directly. They concern property assessments, utility fees, eminent-domain compensation, prevailing wages, state taxes, or other unrelated subjects.

controlling_findings: Idaho Constitution article VII, section 6 requires legislative investment of municipal taxing power.

The Idaho Supreme Court holds that the general local-self-government grant in Idaho Code section 50-301 is not a general taxing grant and that municipal taxes on the public require specific legislative authorization.
Idaho Constitution article III, section 19 prohibits local or special laws for the assessment and collection of taxes, closing the uncodified municipality-specific special-law path.

The only current general-law city local-option nonproperty tax grant found, Idaho Code sections 50-1044 through 50-1049, enumerates short-term lodging occupancy, liquor/wine/beer by the drink, and sales taxes; it does not include wages or compensation.
The complete current code corpus contains no specific grant for a municipal percentage tax on employee wages, earnings, compensation, or payroll.
